items.title: SharpLink 3.0 热路径 0GC：分配审计、优化清单与完整 RPC 语义验收
items.description: ## 目标与定位 在 SharpLink 3.0 保留完整、高性能 RPC 能力的前提下，推动**声明支持范围内的热路径零托管分配（0 managed allocation）**。启动、配置构建、连接/握手、生成代码和冷准备允许分配；普通请求处理、真实异步等待、稳定背压和流 item 处理不能靠重新命名为“冷路径”逃避验收。 用户允许调整现有 API/语义，但新语义必须明确、可安全使用、资源有界，并保持良好的 RPC 行为。本 issue 是目标、优化候选与验收账本，**不是声明当前已实现 0GC，也不是提前批准所有候选方案**。不能给尚未测试的项目填预计 B/op 收益。 ### 与 3.0 主架构的关系 - 与 [#999](https://github.com/SunSi12138/SharpLink/issues/999) 的原生双端版本协商、安全热切换、统一 RPC 分派共同推进；协议/身份/接收者选择仍由 #999 统筹。本 issue 不预选 N、Q2、S 或 Hybrid，不替换 #999 的 M/F/V 正确性义务。 - leased/owning、Task/ValueTask、context/cancellation 等形式必须进入同一个可审计 RPC 核心；不得建立绕过 registration/method facts/auth/tenant/准入安全的“0GC raw 旁路”。 - 公开 API/Generated ABI/wire 变更与 #999、[#805](https://github.com/SunSi12138/SharpLink/issues/805) 一起审核；存储所有权变化不自动等于需要改 wire，是否改动须逐项决定。 - 不修改或抬高现有 allocation budget 来宣告优化成功；已有语义测试、失败证据和发布门禁继续有效。 ## 证据基线与可信度 - 审计及建 issue 时复核的 dev HEAD：[`2948de82fff77d66fce51ecec9a5783b6ef3cb62`](https://github.com/SunSi12138/SharpLink/commit/2948de82fff77d66fce51ecec9a5783b6ef3cb62)。 - 当前主工程/benchmark 是 net10.0 传统 async lowering。每次实施前重新记录实际 SHA、SDK、runtime patch、OS/CPU/架构、GC 模式、transport 和功能组合；固定链接只证明上述基线。 - 本轮获得的是源码审计，**没有该 HEAD 成功完成的新增端到端分配实测**。[对应 CI](https://github.com/SunSi12138/SharpLink/actions/runs/43689267594) 的 allocation-trend job 为 skipped；本地门禁因执行环境问题未运行成功。二者都不是 PASS。 - 旧 `doc/performance.md`、P2/P3 报告和非发布实验 profile 只能按其实际 SHA/场景引用，不能当作当前 HEAD 数值。 - 证据标签：**源码确定**＝存在实际可达的分配操作；**条件确定**＝满足真实挂起/功能开关/容量边界时发生；**待归因**＝需 probe/trace 证明是否、何时、由哪层分配。普通 `new struct`、同步完成的 ValueTask、每连接一次的长期循环不自动算作每 RPC 分配。 当前 [allocation-budgets.json](https://github.com/SunSi12138/SharpLink/blob/2948de82fff77d66fce51ecec9a5783b6ef3cb62/eng/perf/allocation-budgets.json) 的允许中位数上限如下，**它们不是实测值**： | Case | 上限 B/op | | --- | ---: | | rpc-add-sharedmemory-c1 | 1450 | | rpc-add-sharedmemory-c8 | 650 | | rpc-oneway-sharedmemory-c1 | 960 | | send-pump-idle-wake-balanced | 700 | ### 已有基础，避免重复造轮子或错误归因 - Generated request 已是 readonly struct，经 `in` 泛型通道调用；proxy 构造期缓存 codec；没有每调用 object[]/反射分派这一前提。 - Unary pending 已是池化 `RpcRequestOperation /IValueTaskSource `；普通 timed Unary 使用连接共享 deadline scheduler，不是每调用 Task.Delay/CTS。 - plain timed Unary/OneWay 不必创建 shared ClientLogicalCallState；多参与者/stream/interceptor 路径另计。 - 普通 timed Unary 使用 pending failure observer，不自动创建 observeEmission TCS；标准 request 的 pending/send-queue 满载默认是 fail-fast。 - `TransportConnection.AwaitReadAsync` 已使用 pooling builder；WakeupSignal 的普通 untimed 已注册等待使用可复用 IThreadPoolWorkItem。 - 已有 generation lease、stable mailbox、publication gate、物理 tail、buffe

items.title: Monitoring, slice 1, part C2: the monitoring stage, its pages, the dead-man ping and the clock's watch
items.description: ## Why A stored halt is sent with no alarm, because the receive loop leaves that to monitoring (`runtime/loop/receive.py:1023`), and no monitoring component exists in `src/`. `data/spikes.py` stores each move and below-the-low flag on the snapshot, and nothing reads them. Nothing pings a dead-man check. So no shadow decision may send an order, and no deploy may run unattended, before this part. The record of splits now exists (`data/splits.csv`, PR #243), so hard limit 3's second exception no longer applies in code: `LakeSource` loads the record on every read and halts when it cannot (`data/source.py:283-290`). #242 rewrites the limit's text. The move flag's alert is still owed, because the owner ruled on 2026-11-22 on #5 that a flag alerts rather than halts, and design.md's rule that a split reads as neither a gain nor a loss, under `### A backtest names what it could not have traded, and each model states how it fails`, names three kinds of unrecorded split that only the move flag catches. The plan passes on #201 derived this text against `main` at `40aa53e`, and every line number below is at that commit. The argument for the split, and the order of the four parts, stay on #201. ## What must hold ### 1. The stage and its pages No monitoring component exists. Stage names are `core/names.py:54-69`, and `Monitoring` appears only in comments that promise it. 07-deployment.md's `## Where it runs` gives it a container per deployment, and its grant rows. design.md's `### Rule 7: monitoring tells the owner once` sets the rules. Monitoring is a stage of its own, the last of each decision: it reads every stage's result for that decision, pages, stores its result and pings (05-building-blocks.md's flow, and 06-runtime.md's `#### Finish, once per decision`). So it gains a row in the stage table that `runtime/loop/table.py` declares, the routes generated from that table change in the same commit, and the supervisor's run stop, which waits for every stage's result for every decision (`runtime/supervisor/__init__.py:33-35`), waits for monitoring's too. The decision's report, which 08-crosscutting-concepts.md's `#### Decision reports` says monitoring writes before the ping, is #204's to add to this stage, and the ping waits for it once #204 builds it. Rule 7 also says monitoring journals every halt. items.title: P1 — Measure game-origin storage accurately for Network & Storage
items.description: ## Current assignment — 2026-11-28 **Owner:** Chaty (`agent:chaty`). #10 persistent network totals and #228 addon archive/runtime limits are merged. Chaty is now investigating a trustworthy game-origin storage measurement to complete the Network & Storage page in #248. ## Goal Display one game data-size value in launcher Settings without counting unrelated launcher data or exposing GeckoView internals incorrectly. ## Constraints - Never clear, migrate, copy, rename, compact, or otherwise mutate the GeckoView profile. - Do not report `filesDir`, cacheDir, codeCacheDir, all app-private storage, GeckoView profile size, APK size or the full application data footprint as “game size”. - Do not claim origin-specific usage unless it is measured for the actual game origin using a supported GeckoView/Web API. - No telemetry, analytics, or external upload. - Treat unsupported or unavailable storage APIs as “Not available”; never guess. - Keep this independent from #148 Activity/window orientation work and preserve the current GeckoSession/profile. ## Investigation / implementation - Inspect the repository's pinned GeckoView API and the game's actual origin/storage mode. - Check whether `navigator.storage.estimate()` is available/reliable in the active game origin and whether the result can be read safely using the current GeckoSession API without replacing or navigating away from the session. - If supported, expose an explicit origin-scoped storage estimate with a clear label and caveat that the browser's estimate is approximate and origin-scoped (not the whole game download or all cache). - If unsupported or no durable game-origin quota exists, keep the value unavailable and document the limitation rather than presenting app totals as game size. - Add deterministic tests for available/unavailable, error, and invalid/negative estimate states. ## Acceptance criteria - The Settings page shows only Game data size as the storage metric. - The value is grounded in a documented supported API for the actual game origin, or the UI clearly reports unavailable. - The code never deletes/changes profile contents and does not mislabel unrelated app storage. - Exact-head formatting, lint, build and unit tests pass. ## Integration #248 owns the Network & Storage screen. Chaty will integrate the result there.

items.title: Evaluate a turn-end model for when a spoken request is over
items.description: ## Problem A request ends after a fixed 0.7 s of silence (`audio.end_silence_s`). A clear command then waits the full 0.7 s, and a hesitant one is cut off when the owner pauses longer. ## What the code shows - `audio.end_silence_s` (default 0.7) with Silero VAD decides the end of speech (`docs/models.md`, "Wake word and end of speech"). - 0.7 s is what other local assistants use, so it is not a defect. - A turn-end model judges from the audio whether the speaker has finished: Smart Turn v3 (BSD-2-Clause, about 8 MB, 13 to 95 ms on a CPU per its project). Not verified on this project's audio. - Starting the transcription early (at 0.3 s of silence) would save about 0.4 s but wastes a GPU run each time the owner pauses mid-sentence. ## Plan 1. Score Smart Turn on recorded requests (`jarvis speech-test record` sets) against the fixed threshold: how often each cuts a request off, and the time saved. 2. Build it only if it wins, as an option first, with its licence and pin checked (`add-dependency-or-voice` skill). ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Measurement recorded in `docs/models.md`. - [ ] Decision recorded here.

items.title: Let the owner interrupt Jarvis by voice with echo cancellation
items.description: ## Deliverable The owner can interrupt Jarvis by voice while it speaks ("Hey Jarvis, stop"), without Jarvis triggering itself from its own voice. ## Decisions - 2026-11-20 (plan, from the Codex review): v1 suspends wake detection during speech and interrupts only by keybinding (`jarvis stop`); voice barge-in needs echo cancellation first. ## Constraints - Later phase (`docs/plan.md` → Phases 7): starts after the voice milestone and Spotify are working. - Policy, provenance and silence rules from `AGENTS.md` apply; agent tests run silent, real-audio checks with the owner. - Echo cancellation through PipeWire's echo-cancel module (or equivalent) so speaker output is removed from the mic signal; spoken confirmation stays disabled for `strong` actions regardless. - Self-trigger test: Jarvis saying "Hey Jarvis" through the speakers must not wake it. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Echo-cancelled capture path, selectable in config, documented in `docs/playbook/`. - [ ] Self-trigger and barge-in measured with the owner (false triggers per hour of Jarvis speech; interrupts detected out of 50). ## Review additions (2026-11-20) - PipeWire 1.6.9 with the echo-cancel and WebRTC AEC libraries is installed; a working echo-cancel graph and its accuracy are unverified. Voice interruption is an addition; the v1 `jarvis stop` keybinding stays. - Document an owner-run setup (playback reference, echo-cancel source, output device, fixed clips). An accepted stop drains or cancels queued output and returns to the wake state without opening confirmation. Test cancel, device loss and fallback to the keybinding; `strong` stays keybinding-only. - Open: thresholds. Recommendation zero self-triggers in the recorded test and an owner-approved detection and latency target before enabling. - [ ] Owner run records false triggers per hour, trigger latency and interrupts detected out of 50, including playback of Jarvis saying "Hey Jarvis". ## Related - Extends #3 and #6; shares the speaker drain and stop contract with #12 and #18.

items.title: Continue upstream-first port rollout across the backlog
items.description: ## Current rollout scope · Revision 4, November 20, 2026 Make the full eligible catalog maintainable through shared capabilities and automatic upstream updates. A capability is complete when its producer, Core behavior and clients work, every fitting consumer has migrated, a capable released client receives the change, and ordinary maintenance and recovery run through existing workers. Retire the manual authoring path after cutover. Preserve historical definitions, installed runtime identity, pins and player data. One Astra owner integrates bounded Sol implementation work and independent non-writing review. The owner retains checks, guarded merge, protected publication, release, client readback and reconciliation. Capture the implementation/platform inventory and source cursors once, then reconcile changes through cutover. Keep known mandatory failures scoped to their operations and continue independent work during waits. Existing signing, artifact admission and resource budgets govern every delivery. #177 and #2100 own discovery and natural scheduled evidence. #8417 owns maintenance resource and recovery acceptance. #246 owns ordered frozen-client delivery, including correction and recovery. #315 owns independent curated-byte admission. #8384 owns mod loaders and original-file behavior, #8115 retains its provider scope and #8076 owns game-first released-client acceptance. Existing settings, artwork, platform and managed-operation commitments retain their owners. [Pickup inventory and cursors](https://github.com/boburning/portcove/issues/1422#issuecomment-7057012134). ## Unified adoption and capability ownership — October 29, 2026 UTC Port integration is the primary product outcome: discover upstream/game/release/platform → evaluate the useful route → reuse existing Core/adapters, official packages, supported upstream preparation or safe existing-installation registration → identify the exact unsupported operation → prioritize against concrete consumers → implement only justified missing behavior through its existing owner → apply it to all fitting consumers → validate offered operations and deliver/reconcile canonical records. items.title: Monitoring, slice 1, part C1: the alert channel, its forwarder, and the alarm every page is built from
items.description: ## Why Hard limit 3 says a missing or stale input halts trading **and alerts the owner**. At `40aa53e` the one `Alerts` adapter is `adapters/alerts.py`'s `LogAlerts`, a stand-in that writes `ALARM : ` to standard error and reaches no person. This part builds the route from every process to the owner's phone, and the alarm every page is built from. #258's monitoring stage and #259's schedule checks page through it. The plan passes on #201 derived this text against `main` at `40aa53e`, and every line number below is at that commit. The argument for the split, and the order of the four parts, stay on #201. ## What must hold 1. **One ntfy topic per environment**, separate from marketlake's and from each other's, on the owner's phone (design.md `### 2026-11-06`, entries 1 and 3). The host's provisioning step writes its address from `/ithildin/ /heartbeat/` to memory-backed storage at boot (07-deployment.md's `## Where it runs`). Every environment, live included, uses ntfy's free public server, and no paid tier is bought (owner ruling of 2026-11-27 on #201). So a topic's name stays its only password on every environment, kept as a secret that enters no tracked file. 2. **Two routes reach the topic, and only two processes hold its address.** 06-runtime.md's row 14.2 puts the crossing at monitoring, and `docs/halts-and-drills.md`'s `### What each environment drills as it arrives` lets only the monitoring role and the VM role read the address. design.md's `### Rule 7: monitoring tells the owner once` sends every alarm raised outside monitoring by the host's direct route. 1. **Monitoring posts its own pages**, through an adapter behind `core.ports.Alerts`. 2. **Every other process writes its alarm to the host's journal**, as `LogAlerts` does now, through each `LogAlerts` `runtime/entry.py` builds: each worker at `:516`, the supervisor at `:568` and a refused setting at `:448`. A forwarder on the host, beside the `OnFailure` handler, reads those lines from the runtime's units and posts each. When a push is refused it writes a marker, which #258's monitoring reads before each dead-man ping. This part builds the forwarder's code, as an entry point of the same image, and #202 its unit, which runs the pinned digest. So the line a release writes and the forwarder that reads it ship together, and a rollback moves both. A forwarder that restarts must not drop the lines written while it was down. items.title: Close secrets-on-read and output-condensing hook gaps across harnesses
items.description: ## Problem Factory's retired instruction rules assumed hooks cover secrets on read and command output condensing across harnesses. Audit and close the coverage gaps without reintroducing prose rules. ## Audit - Claude registers `rtk hook claude` for Bash and `~/.claude/hooks/sonar-secrets/build-scripts/pretool-secrets.sh` for Read in `~/.claude/settings.json`. - Codex registers Factory's `command_guard` for Bash and a prompt-secrets hook in `~/.codex/hooks.json`, but no secrets-on-read or rtk output-condensing hook was found there. Recognition of rtk wrappers by command_guard does not itself condense output. - OpenCode has `~/.config/opencode/plugins/rtk.ts`, which attempts command rewriting when rtk is available; runtime activation and its coverage require verification. No equivalent secrets-on-read registration was identified in the inspected OpenCode configuration and plugins. ## Acceptance Verify each harness's actual supported hook capabilities and runtime registration, then close or explicitly document the missing secrets-on-read and output-condensing coverage for Codex and OpenCode with reproducible tests. Do not expose secret values in evidence.

items.title: Unreal: den låga vintersolen är neutralvit, webbens är varmt orange
items.description: Lapp: Varmare vintersol Del av #2242. Den låga vintersolen den 24 december kl. 14 färgar tegelväggen och fönsterkarmarna tydligt orange och rosa på webben. I Unreal är solljuset neutralt, efter att solskuggorna rättades i #2386 (554cd47e). Webbens karmar ser laxrosa ut i solen, Unreals vita. ![Webben](https://github.com/solwation/lunden-3d-apartment/blob/554cd47e6200dbb4c03cea53a8521f52014e7745/docs/verification/2386/web-patio-christmas.jpg?raw=true) ![Unreal](https://github.com/solwation/lunden-3d-apartment/blob/554cd47e6200dbb4c03cea53a8521f52014e7745/docs/verification/2386/unreal-patio-christmas.jpg?raw=true) #2384 gäller lampljus, inte solen. items.title: Overview cards: the linked line and the combine note sit on the title's line
items.description: From the stakeholder's look at the joined cards in the mock, 2026-11-28 (screenshot: `Veg [Parent]` with "Zone: Nursery is linked to this zone" on a line of its own beneath, and `Nursery` with "Linked to Zone: Veg" beneath): "zone text needs to be in line with title so stuff isnt pushed Down (average also needs to occupy this space" ## What that means - On an Overview card the linked text sits on the same line as the zone's name (name and `Parent` badge at the left, the grey text in the space to their right), so a linked card's readings start at the same height as any other card's. - The note that says how a zone's sensors were combined ("Average of 2 sensors" and the like) uses that same space on the title's line, not a line of its own. - Cards in a row keep lining up: the day strip and the tracks start at the same height on every card, linked or not, combined or not. - Where the line cannot hold it all (a narrow card, a long name) it may wrap, but nothing is cut off or overlapped. Mock first, on the combined preview. Builds on #90 and #88.

items.title: Plugin install sources beyond github.com (generic git and local directory)
items.description: Part of #2920 Depends on: #2921 ## Problem Plugin install accepts only github.com URLs. A plugin on another git host (for example a self-hosted GitLab or Gitea) cannot install. `/plugin install` cannot use a local plugin directory. ## Evidence (dev/0.9.x, c08187058e) - `src-tauri/src/services/skill_service/github.rs:31-32`: other hosts fail with `Only github.com repository URLs are supported`. - `src-tauri/src/services/skill_service/importing.rs:282-289`: the download uses `codeload.github.com` or `api.github.com` zipball. - `src-tauri/src/services/skill_service/importing.rs:243-249`: the local skill import accepts `.skill`, `.zip`, or a directory, but this path is not connected to `/plugin install`. ## Proposed approach 1. Accept a generic git URL (`https://...git`, with an optional ref). Use a shallow clone or the host archive URL. Keep the current zip safety checks (`extract_zip_secure`). 2. Accept a local directory path for `/plugin install` and for the Skills view, with the same preview and hook approval. 3. Keep the github.com fast path. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A plugin on a non-GitHub git host installs with the same preview and approval flow. - [ ] `/plugin install /path/to/plugin` installs a local plugin in session scope. - [ ] github.com install behavior does not change.

items.title: bridge: 턴 중간에 본문을 그대로 보내는 도구(send_to_user) — 도구 호출 사이 긴 글이 요약 메모로 바뀌어 버블 본문이 빠짐 (#2161 후속)
items.description: ## 요약 에이전트가 도구 호출 사이에 쓴 긴 글(붙여넣기용 본문, 표, 정확한 값)이 채널에 **본문 대신 2~3줄 요약으로** 도착하는 일이 반복됩니다. 브리지나 봇이 떨어뜨린 것이 아니라 현재 모델 세대의 API 동작이고, 요약 전 원문은 API가 돌려주지 않아 브리지 설정으로는 되살릴 수 없습니다. 턴 중간에 본문을 그대로 보내는 도구(`send_to_user`)를 브리지가 에이전트에게 제공하도록 제안합니다. #2161 후속입니다. ## 실측 (gwakga, 한데, 2026-11-28 KST, `claude-fable-5-2`) 오너에게 노드별 지시문을 버블 하나씩 보내는 작업이었습니다. 버블마다 도구 호출 하나를 사이에 두었습니다. 봇 저널(`native-relay-bot`의 `agent_outbound kind=interim` `bytes`)과 세션 기록(`~/.claude/projects/…/ .jsonl`)을 대조했습니다. | 시각 | 버블 | 쓴 본문 | 실제 전송 | 세션 기록의 블록 | |---|---|---|---|---| | 11:15:33 | 1 | 2,209 B | 2,209 B | `text` | | 11:15:41 | 2 | 1,939 B | **295 B** | `thinking` 297 B + `tool_use` (text 없음) | | 11:15:51 | 3 | 2,652 B | 2,652 B | `text` | | 11:15:59 | 4 | 1,622 B | **174 B** | `thinking` 176 B + `tool_use` | | 11:16:11 ~ 11:17:06 | 5 ~ 10 | 2,681 ~ 3,126 B | 같은 크기 | `text` | | 11:22:40 | 4 재전송 | 1,769 B | **178 B** | `thinking` 180 B + `tool_use` | | 11:34:12 | 4 재재전송 | 1,621 B | **395 B** | `thinking` 397 B + `tool_use` | | 11:34:40 · 11:34:56 | 11 · 12 | 2,689 · 2,663 B + 머리말 | 2,957 · 2,760 B | `text` | | 11:35:12 | 안내 4줄 | 약 900 B | **270 B** | `thinking` 272 B + `tool_use` | - 중간 버블 15개 중 **5개**가 요약으로 바뀌었습니다. 같은 본문(4번)은 세 번 연속으로 바뀌어, 다시 보내는 것으로는 해결되지 않았습니다. - 바뀐 버블은 모두 세션 기록에 `text` 블록이 없고, 비어 있지 않은 `thinking` 블록과 `tool_use`만 있습니다. 전송 바이트는 그 `thinking` 텍스트에서 앞뒤 공백을 뺀 크기와 같습니다(#2161의 진행 메모 경로가 그대로 전달한 것). - 턴의 **마지막 답**으로 보낸 같은 본문은 매번 그대로 도착했습니다. - 이 세션 전체로는 `text` 48 · 비어 있지 않은 `thinking` 44 · `tool_use` 169 블록입니다. - 받는 쪽에서는 본문 자리에 「…몫 4건을 정리했어요」 같은 한 줄만 보이므로 누락인지 알기 어렵습니다. 에이전트 쪽도 보낸 것으로 알고 넘어갑니다. ## 원인 Claude API 이행 안내서(Claude Opus 5.5 · Claude Fable 5.1 절 「Text between tool calls comes back in thinking blocks」)의 동작 그대로입니다. - 이 세대 모델에서는 도구 호출 사이에 쓴 글이 한두 문장을 넘으면 `text`가 아니라 **진행 메모용 `thinking` 블록**(도구 호출 앞에 최대 1개)으로 돌아오고, 그 텍스트는 짧은 요약입니다. - #2161이 이 블록을 사용자에게 보이는 진행 메모로 전달하게 했습니다. 내레이션에는 맞는 동작이지만, 본문 전달에는 쓸 수 없습니다. - `thinking.display` 값을 바꿔도 요약 전 원문은 돌아오지 않습니다. - 안내서의 권고: 턴 중간에 사용자에게 **그대로** 보여야 하는 내용이 있으면 사용자에게 메시지를 보내는 도구를 주라는 것입니다. 도구 입력은 요약되지 않습니다(같은 안내서 「Add a `send_to_user` tool for verbatim mid-task delivery」). ## 제안 브리지가 에이전트에게 도구 하나를 제공합니다. - **이름 · 입력**: `send_to_user(message: string)`. 방이나 대상 인자는 없습니다. - **동작**: 현재 턴이 답하고 있는 그 대화(방 · 채팅)에 `message`를 중간 버블로 보냅니다. 기존 중간 버블 경로(`interim_message_callback`, 한데는 `interim` 프레임)를 그대로 쓰고, 제어 문자 정리(`_clean_response`) 외에는 내용을 바꾸지 않습니다. - **결과**: 전송 여부와 크기를 돌려줍니다(예: `delivered`, `bytes`, `parts`). 실패는 사유 코드로 돌려줍니다 — 활성 턴 없음, 길이 초과, 턴당 중간 버

items.title: Ask HN: Anthropic is accusing my company of distilling. How can I prove I'm not?
items.description: Basically the title. Anthropic is accusing me and my company of using their API for distillation. We are not. We do not train our own models. Our only usage which I think could get us flagged is automated regression benchmarks whenever we change some AI settings. But this is not against their policy? Now I've got 24h to prove we didn't. Has anyone dealt with this too? How can you prove that you are not distilling Anthropic models without breaking your user's privacy?

items.title: Ask HN: Users asking to remove their commits under GDPR
items.description: Seeing a spike of people asking to remove their commits from open-source GitHub repositories that I am the owner of because those commits carry their personal email or other identifiers. How are you handling these?

items.title: Ask HN: Any courses/products by indie makers worth getting today?
items.description: Though I am not a JS dev, I got threejs-journey (no affiliation with the creator) last year on a whim, enjoyed it. Any courses/products/books etc that you recommend, specifically from Indie makers? Not interested in big promotions like Udemy, Datacamp etc

items.title: Ask HN: Where is all the amazing AI-generated software?
items.description: I feel like the most amazing thing about AI so far is AI itself. Is anyone using a brand-new tool that was not available 5 years ago? I see people decompiling/reverse engineering the Adobe suite, which is an amazing feat, but the resulting software itself is barely usable. Since it’s so easy to build anything now, I get a sense we’re seeing a proliferation of one-off, proof-of-concept projects, where great software takes time and effort and often multiple people, AI notwithstanding.

items.title: Ask HN: How do you find meaning of life at 41?
items.description: Happy Thanksgiving! This question crossed my mind in the morning. It feels like I have seen pretty much everything under the Sun. I have modest house (still renting), small kids, a okayish job. I spent time on daily activities and occassionally on long walks. The progress with AI and impact on Software is frankly exciting and depressing at the same time. What are people my age doing these days? How do you keep yourself excited for the future and not feel anxious? Curious to see from a bit older people here how are you doing and challenging yourself well into 40s, 50s and 60s.

items.title: Ask HN: Coworker rejects PR (a month in) because it does not meet his standards
items.description: just joined this new team about 1 year into their development. Demoed the work to the team about two weeks ago (half way in). Work is practically complete & runs well no issues. I create PR & assign the two PR reviewers (one my rank another a rank above me). one colleague (the one at my level) leaves some constructive comments no functional changes. The other colleague (one rank above me) says something equivalent to "does not meet our standards" "do not do x pattern since we have used y (which has a huge limitation)" to use Y pattern I would basically need to change most of the logic and it would be about 70% waste. I demoed my code with this pattern two weeks ago and there were no issues/comments from the team. The code is concise and easy to read. I had a call with the colleague and explained the code and why I used it, and showed him some other parts of the codebase where this pattern should be used, his only defense was that "it does not meet our standards because it uses X rather than y pattern, since we used y pattern in the past, we should only use y pattern" while x pattern is very similar only removing the limitation that was causing the code to be difficult to maintain etc. This "standard requirement" is written nowhere as a hard requirement and the codebase is barely one year old, with only one of the codebase founders still on the team.... I'm going to have a chat with the manager tomorrow morning.

items.title: Ask HN: Would you care for more than 2FA for any of your accounts?
items.description: Infrastructure has been hacked way too many times and some how the Uno Reverse solution was to put onus on users to choose a more complex password that the user would not have used anywhere else in the past (hence password managers came to existence). Then some services added/mandated the support for requiring one additional authentication method, hence the term 2FA. As a user do you feel comfortable with that level of security or would you rather want to choose the number of authentication methods for your account based on the sensitivity of the service? In other words is 2FA good enough or would you prefer to have more.

items.title: Ask HN: How well do you understand what's going on inside RL?
items.description: Reinforcement learning: you see it all the time in the context of LLMs and chess agents. We often hear that it trains on rewards without labeled data, but how much of the actual algorithms under the hood could you explain?

items.title: Ask HN: How do you handle corporate life?
items.description: I recently started in a 18000people corporation. I am wondering how people are dealing with corporate life? I am suddenly in a more consulting role, and people from IT tell me to not be too motivated, as the last people with my naive vision quit quite fast when they hit roadblocks everywhere. I read the submission about flailing recently, and while i can relate about having lots of parallel strategies, i am struggling with the human aspect. people talk about so much empty stuff and just push slides back and forth. how do you come to terms with this?

items.title: Ask HN: Why can AI prove Riemann but not solve cust svc problems?
items.description: I’m genuinely curious on perspectives here. My hunch is some of the answers might imply the existential risk to humanity is not quite what it seems. My hypothesis is that you need both verifiability and a domain-native semantic model/self-contained symbolic universe. Those conditions don’t hold for a lot of human activity. I think the corollary to this hypothesis is whether semantic model construction itself is verifiable, in which many more domains will start to look like coding and math.

items.title: Ask HN: Am I the only one whose AI hype is cooling down a lot?
items.description: I am in the industry for 15+ years, studied CS, and actually, never really "liked" programming. It was a means to an end. I have written about programming (and published books), so don't get me wrong: I like the craft and I miss the sense of accomplishment after hours and days of struggling and fixing a problem with 2 lines of code. What I see in my personal spending and habits: I get free tokens from my company, and I spent between 3k-5k a month at the start of the year. Models got cheaper, but also: The usefullness ran its course a little bit for me. I still don't write code by hand, but when doing research, finding solutions, even some decisions (using Opus 5.5 and Astra 6.2 for example) are more and more questionable. I handed large research tasks to models, but even small questions like: "What do you think about these PR comments pointing out issues" (I need to be vague, working for a larger company), it didn't find even basic facts I found via Google and reading the docs for 2mins. I usually did higher level thinking, researched with the model, and then went to the implementation phase. But lately, I am not happy with both the research results (I continuesly have to narrow it down, go back, refine... I spend a day or 2 days refining, which in the end, I can do by myself now and actually feel a sense of accomplishment). Even the implementation isn't all that great. Maybe my bar for acceptable work is higher now, since these tools are not "magic" anymore. I think I gave them more leeway in the beginning because they wowed me. But now... not so much anymore. I even dread opening up Claude Code or Codex and I'd rather read and write code myself, and just give them smaller tasks, or once I nailed it down, I let a large chunk of code write by a model (because it "types" faster...). Am I alone? I read a lot of think pieces, I have agents working on my private dedicated server to maintain my machine and set up my self-hosting services. But more and more, I'd rather.... do it myself again, be more precise, and use it as a workhorse instead of a thinking researcher.

items.title: Ask HN: Security for the Small Developer
items.description: I’m overloaded with the amount of information about what I could be doing to secure myself and with how terrible things are about to become, or so they say. Do I need to spend hours and hours securing myself or are there some basic things I could do that would be good enough? And I’m talking about things like securing my laptop and my Web server and my Gmail and my passwords. Do I need a physical key? What if I’m a kind of person who loses things like that? Do I need tailscale? Is there a simple pattern I can follow here?

items.title: Ask HN: If you had no limitations what would you build in AI?
items.description: - You know the field, even if you are not a top expert. - You know a group of investors who believe in you and will back your next move. - Your idea could be implemented with technology that exists today or could exist in the near future. Please, explain why it fits with the premisses. What would you build?

items.title: Ask HN: Everything will get breached. How do you limit the blast radius?
items.description: Got another breach email this morning, this travel operator had my passport number and travel history stored. At this point I feel every service we use is going to get dumped eventually. I consider unique passwords and hardware 2FA as no brainers, they stop credential stuffing, but they don't help when a service leaks your actual identity. There are just so many services that require personal data like your passport number, phone number etc. And I think the fallout will only get worse as agentic workflows and local models become more mainstream and people start giving them more and more personal data. Assuming every vendor database is basically public eventually, how are you actually limiting the blast radius without turning everyday life into a massive faff?

items.title: Ask HN: For professional Mathematicians –- about your career in the future
items.description: Hi friends, genuine question. We all see that top notch Mathematicians can use LLM to prove world class results in a relatively short time of period. OK I admit some of the results are not verified yet, but please hear me. Neither do I know how much “brain” is human and how much is the LLM, because we don’t see the prompts. My question is: what do you think about your career in the future? Please hear me out. In the current world, the way you become a Mathematician, is to get good scores, go to schools, take PHD and then professorship. There may be middle steps like postdoctoral or industry experience, but that’s the general way to do it. And the way that schools judge professors, if I understand correctly, is more about how much results you can get —- ofc if you can obtain big grants then the better, but most of you can’t do that, so I assume that it’s more about the papers. You also teach but that’s not as big as the research. For now, there are a lot of smaller problems left to solve, and since world class Mathematicians tend to devote their life to one world class problem, there are plenty of food for everyone. Does the above make sense? This leads me to the question of: if the future of getting proofs is to prompt with an LLM or whatever AI solution, and it is apparent that world class Mathematicians can prove more conjectures or whatever than they ever can dream without LLM, why do schools need mediocre Mathematicians? I’m not trying to belittle you, but I’m trying to figure out career paths for my son, and I need to understand the impact of AI to all career paths. Again, I iterate, if one world class Mathematicians can prompt through many problems in their lifetime, we face two possibilities: 1. LLMs are good at solving problems but not good at asking new questions, so eventually we have few questions to crack, so the world doesn’t really need that many Mathematicians. 2. LLM is equally good at asking new questions. Well again I don’t see why the school needs to hire so many Mathematicians. Again, I believe LLM is merely the tool here, you still need the Mathematicians to do the thinking —- this does NOT contradict what I wrote. Of course, there is another part of your work, that is to teach Mathematics. But I’m not sure that is unique to humans. Maybe LLM can do that too. It just needs more training on that because so far the training is more on proving things, not teaching things. I want to iterate a third time, that I’m not belittling you. You ar
